newsitem.title: USA: Perkin-Elmer to take FY97 charge.
newsitem.headline: Perkin-Elmer to take FY97 charge.

text.p: Perkin-Elmer Corp said Tuesday it expected to take a charge against earnings for fiscal year 1997 for the second phase of a reorganization to make its operations more efficient.
A spokeswoman for the company said the charge will be less than the $71.6 million restructuring charge registered for fiscal 1996.
Perkin-Elmer also said it planned to cut about 285 manufacturing jobs in the United States and Europe as part of a plan to improve efficiency.
The company said it would cut jobs at its facilities in Llantrisant, Wales; Uberlingen, Germany; and Norwalk, Connecticut.
A spokeswoman said Norwalk would suffer the deepest cut with 170 jobs lost.
She said the company would be cutting jobs throughout fiscal 1998, which is to begin on July 1.

"The remainder of the program's cost savings will come from increased productivity achieved through outsourcing and higher utilization of the company's Singapore facility," the company said in a statement.
The outsourcing of specific manufacturing functions will be implemented during fiscal year 1998, it added.
Perkin-Elmer began the plan in early calendar 1996.

"This reorganization should improve our profitability and position us to compete more effectively in the marketplace by reducing our asset base, reducing inventories, improving cash flow, and converting fixed expenses to variable expenses," it said.
Perkin-Elmer makes analytical instruments for the pharmaceutical industry, among other things.
